Config requirements are stage specific in [cli.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/inbound/cli.rs).

| Command | YAML type | Fields | Environment |
|---|---|---|---|
| latest, copy-latest-raw | `LoaderConfig` | `data_dir` | None |
| declarations fetch | `DeclarationFetcherConfig` | `data_dir`, `batch_size` | `DATABASE_URL` |
| declarations clean | `LoaderConfig` | `data_dir` | None |
| declarations resolve | `DeclarationResolverConfig` | `data_dir`, optional `candidate_budget` | None |
| declarations load | `LoaderConfig` | `data_dir` | `DATABASE_URL` |
| members fetch | `FetcherConfig` | `data_dir`, `batch_size` | None |
| members load | `LoaderConfig` | `data_dir` | `DATABASE_URL` |

[config.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/inbound/cli/config.rs) owns YAML deserialization. Every field is required except `candidate_budget`, whose default is `1_000_000`. Unknown YAML keys are accepted because none of the structs uses `deny_unknown_fields`. `batch_size` parses as `u8`, but zero is rejected later by `ParliamentApiClient::new`, which stores `NonZeroU8`. `candidate_budget` parses as `usize` and is checked positive by `TryFrom`, outside serde.

The existing [response_help.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/inbound/cli/response_help.rs:10) generates draft 2020-12 schemas using serialization mode and handler return types. It never invokes handlers. Configuration types cannot be inferred from those signatures because handlers receive `PathBuf` and parse configuration internally.

A minimal extension is to derive `JsonSchema` on the YAML config types, add a deserialization-mode schema helper, and attach stage-specific configuration sections alongside current response sections. Keep response schema generation in serialization mode. Declare environment requirements separately because `DataConfig` is environment input, not YAML. Use exhaustive matches over the existing stage enums so new stages force help updates.

Two accuracy traps need explicit treatment. A plain `u8` schema permits zero although runtime rejects it. A plain `usize` schema likewise permits zero despite the resolver’s manual check. Schema minimum annotations would document behavior but duplicate those rules. Moving the existing nonzero invariants into config field types would make the schema and parsing share ownership, if that scope is acceptable.

[cli_response_help.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/cli_response_help.rs) already verifies long help without configuration or side effects and short help without schema sections. [common/response_schema.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/common/response_schema.rs) extracts any labeled JSON schema section and builds a validator. Extend those tests with valid configs, missing required fields, zero bounds, omitted resolver budget, and unknown keys to match actual parser behavior. No files changed.
